To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current limits on compressed SUSY spectra from the LHC are not as robust as previously thought, and that the current limits are reduced significantly in certain scenarios, especially for the case of compressed gluino spectra.
The current LHC limits on the compressed spectra are not as strong as they could be due to the lack of consideration of the effect of QCD radiation.

(a) the current limits from LHC searches are not applicable to compressed supersymmetric spectra, (b) the limits on the stop mass are reduced by a factor of 4 for a mass difference of 100 MeV and (c) the limits on squark and gluinos are also reduced by a factor between 2 and 3
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to accurately set limits in compressed spectra.
the question of what is the best way of setting limits when SUSY is compressed and how much room for manoeuvre is there in this scenario.
the limits of the LHC searches for supersymmetry with compressed spectra, and the effects of QCD uncertainties in these searches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LHC has excluded SUSY models with a compressed mass spectrum in which the mass of the next lightest superpartner is less than 300 GeV.
the limits on the stop and squark are very dependent on the mass splitting, and the limits on the gluino mass are not.
the current limits on compressed spectra are not very robust.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for compressed scenarios the limits are not as severe as previously thought.
for compressed spectra the limits on SUSY are reduced by a factor of 2-3.
the limits from monojet searches can be improved by up to an order of magnitude.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current LHC bounds on compressed spectra are significantly weakened.
in the presence of a large mass degeneracy the limits on the stop, squarks and gluino masses can be significantly reduced.
the current LHC limits can be significantly reduced if SUSY has a compressed spectrum.
